reasons: No tests are visible for this file.
The brand name is not escaped, so special characters can break the page.
Matching by part of a name can pick the wrong description.
Failures do not set an error exit code, so scripts cannot detect them.

terms.meaning: the markup language that web pages are written in
a way of turning binary file contents into plain text so it can sit inside another file
corporate identity program, the full set of logo, color, and application designs for one brand

depends_on: core (a sibling module in the same folder, imported by name, not in this packet)

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Imports and first wording table entries
sections.what: Loads the tools for command-line input, files, encoding, and dates, plus the shared brief lookup. Then it starts a table of fixed titles, concepts, purposes, and specs for each deliverable type, such as business card and letterhead.
sections.why: Keeps display wording in one place so the layout code does not need to change when wording does.
sections.watch_out: The lookup depends on these keys matching file names, so a new deliverable needs a new entry here.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Rest of the wording table
sections.what: Continues the same table with apparel, vehicles, envelopes, and folders. Each entry has a title, concept, purpose, and specs.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed description per item keeps the presentation text consistent across brands.
sections.watch_out: The specs text is fixed, so sizes and materials appear on every page whether or not they match the mockup.

sections.name: get_image_base64
sections.title: Encoding an image for embedding
sections.what: Reads an image file and returns its contents as a long line of text. If reading fails, it prints a warning and returns nothing.
sections.why: Lets the HTML file display images without separate image files beside it.
sections.watch_out: Large images make the output file very large, and a failed read falls back to a plain file path that only works on this machine.

sections.name: get_deliverable_info
sections.title: Choosing wording from a file name
sections.what: Looks at a file name and returns the matching wording from the table. If nothing matches, it builds a title from the file name and uses generic text.
sections.why: Lets images named after deliverables get the right text automatically.
sections.watch_out: Matching is by part of the name, so short keys such as car also match words like card; check the titles in the output.

sections.name: generate_html (part 1)
sections.title: Brief lookup and page start
sections.what: Checks that the images folder exists and has PNG files, then loads the brand brief for the industry and style. It starts the page with its document header and title.
sections.why: Likely reason: the brief supplies the mood and style labels shown on the banner.
sections.watch_out: The brand name and industry are inserted into the page without escaping, so unusual characters can break the output.

sections.name: generate_html (part 2)
sections.title: Page style rules, first part
sections.what: Writes the first group of styling rules for the page: the dark background, the hero banner, the heading styles, and the layout for each image block with its rounded corners and shadow.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets the premium dark look the presentation is designed to have.
sections.watch_out: The styles sit inside a text template with doubled braces, so an edit with a single brace will break the page.

sections.name: generate_html (part 3)
sections.title: Page style rules, second part
sections.what: Writes the second group of styling rules: text for titles and descriptions, the small specs tag, the color swatch sizes, the footer, and the layout for small screens.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps text readable and the layout usable on phones.
sections.watch_out: The small-screen rules switch the alternating layout off, so the look on phones differs from desktop.

sections.name: generate_html (part 4)
sections.title: Banner details and image loop start
sections.what: Ends the style rules and writes the hero banner with the brand name, subtitle, and four details: industry, style, mood, and item count. It then writes the section heading and starts going through the images.
sections.why: Gives a quick summary at the top before the reader reaches the images.
sections.watch_out: Industry and style fall back to fixed labels when the brief has no value, so a thin brief shows generic text.

sections.name: generate_html (part 5)
sections.title: Image blocks, footer, and saving
sections.what: For each image, writes a block with the picture, title, concept, purpose, and specs. Then it adds the footer with the brand name and today's date, saves the HTML file, and prints the location.
sections.why: One block per image keeps the presentation in file-name order.
sections.watch_out: The default save location is inside the images folder, so running again overwrites the earlier file with the same name.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Command-line options and launch
sections.what: Defines the brand, industry, style, images folder, and output options, reads them from the command line, and runs the page builder.
sections.why: Lets the page be built from a terminal with a single command.
sections.watch_out: The program never checks whether the page was built, so a failed run still exits as if it succeeded.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Program start when run directly
sections.what: When this file is run as a program, it starts the main routine. When another file imports it, nothing starts.
sections.why: Standard Python pattern that lets other code reuse the functions here.

summary: Builds one self-contained HTML page that shows each corporate identity mockup image with a title, a short concept, a purpose, and a specs line.
purpose: Turns a folder of mockup PNG images into a single web presentation for a brand that can be opened or shared without a server.
why: Likely reason: one HTML file with images embedded inside it is easy to open, move, or send.
how: Reads the brand brief for the chosen industry and style. Lists the PNG files in the images folder in name order. Matches each file name to a description from the built-in table, or builds a generic one. Converts each image into embedded text. Writes a dark hero banner, one block per image, and a footer, then saves the file and prints its location.
inputs: Brand name, industry (defaults to technology), optional style, a folder containing PNG images, and an optional output file path.
outputs: One HTML file. By default it is saved in the images folder with a name built from the brand. The program prints a confirmation line.
risks: The brand name and text are placed into the page without escaping, so unusual characters can break it. Embedded images make the file large. Name matching can pick the wrong title. If the folder is missing or has no PNGs, nothing is written and the program still exits without an error code.
debug: First confirm the images folder exists and contains PNG files. Read any warning about an image that could not be loaded. Open the HTML in a browser to check layout. If a title is wrong, rename the image file so it matches a key in the table.
